structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Cooling and electrical-protection products address physical constraints that rise with rack density.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Electrification and data-center density support demand, but economics remain sensitive to hyperscale capex and capacity utilization.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Thermal management is structurally required, but vendor and architecture substitution remains credible.

discovery-weak-signals.name: AI thermal bottleneck exposure
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Repeated capacity additions and >2 GW deployed cooling indicate direct participation in high-density compute thermal infrastructure.

discovery-weak-signals.name: ecosystem embedding
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Reference-architecture collaboration links nVent cooling capability to broader AI-factory deployment design.

adversarial-red-team.name: capitalAllocation
adversarial-red-team.basis: The 2025 Electrical Products Group acquisition was approximately $1.0B and capacity expansion adds integration/utilization burden.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidenceInflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: Installed cooling and growth validate participation, not durable share or returns.

expectations-execution.name: physical execution
expectations-execution.basis: Installed capacity and repeated manufacturing expansion are observable execution milestones.

expectations-execution.name: forward ramp burden
expectations-execution.basis: The newest site remains a 2027 production commitment rather than current output.

thesisQuality.basis: 2025 sales grew 30% to $3.9B with record backlog, while >2 GW liquid-cooling deployment and repeated capacity expansion evidence real adoption; durable share economics remain unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 filing shows continued operating scale and $256M cash; Investor Day targets 10-13% organic CAGR, ~22% adjusted operating margin and ~95% FCF conversion, but acquisition funding/integration adds leverage and execution burden.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At Sep.25 market data NVT was about $163 with ~$26.4B market cap and ~28x forward P/E, a demanding valuation relative to even strong growth expectations.

catalystScore.basis: Identifiable catalysts include first-half-2027 Blaine liquid-cooling production ramp and pending Maverick integration, both material to data-center exposure but still execution-dependent.

governancePower.basis: Proxy describes board/executive oversight and 2025 portfolio transformation; management has executed divestiture/acquisition actions, though the larger Maverick transaction increases capital-allocation burden.

alignment2036.basis: Electrical protection, power distribution and liquid cooling directly serve durable electrification, grid and high-density compute infrastructure needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Cooling, electrical protection, connections, switchgear and engineered power distribution reuse customer relationships across data centers, utilities and broader infrastructure.

bottleneckControl.basis: More than 2 GW of deployed liquid cooling and repeated capacity expansion show meaningful participation in thermal constraints, but competing vendors/architectures prevent monopoly-bottleneck treatment.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Exposure spans data centers, power utilities and electrification, but returns remain sensitive to infrastructure capex cycles, acquisition integration and capacity utilization.

substitutionResilience.basis: Decade-plus liquid-cooling experience and broad electrical portfolio support qualification persistence, while competing cooling architectures and power vendors remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Global manufacturing scale and active capacity additions provide some redundancy, but current evidence does not establish tested multi-source redundancy for all critical inputs; unknowns cap the score.

pricingPower.basis: Management targets ~22% adjusted operating margins and portfolio differentiation supports value capture, but customer-level price pass-through and new-capacity returns are not disclosed.

riskEvidence.basis: Primary risks are demanding valuation, acquisition/integration burden, hyperscale capex cyclicality, capacity utilization and architecture/vendor substitution.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity, filings, governance, strategy, capacity and transaction facts are current and primary-source backed; confidence is reduced by undisclosed customer concentration/utilization, limited independent operating corroboration and valuation sensitivity.

scoreRecord.thesis: nVent is a scaled electrical-infrastructure supplier with credible participation in AI/data-center cooling and power bottlenecks plus broader electrification exposure; the opportunity is offset by acquisition/capacity execution risk and a valuation that already discounts substantial growth.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A high valuation combined with Maverick integration and liquid-cooling capacity expansion leaves material downside if hyperscale capex, utilization, margins or architecture share disappoint.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Execution against the first-half-2027 Blaine production ramp and evidence that Maverick/backlog converts into profitable growth without balance-sheet or margin deterioration.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the methodology-weighted component score; risk and confidence are separately preserved for runtime gate application rather than silently recomputed with an undocumented formula.
